note: Thursday pre-Asia-open run, 24 Sep 2026 -- latest completed US session is Wed 23 Sep close, which saw a broad equity pullback (S&P -0.76%, Nasdaq -0.69%, Dow -1.03%, Russell2000 -1.28%) with a vol pop (VIX +2.08% to 15.18), snapping the recent vol-compression trend on hawkish Fed commentary and a firmer dollar. Sentiment and breadth confirm the deterioration: CNN Fear & Greed held at 35/Fear on collapsing price-strength/breadth components even as safe-haven demand ticked toward greed, and only ~42%/29% of S&P names sit above their 200-/50-DMA with just Energy closing higher. Crypto's own gauge eased to 71/Greed from a recent Extreme-Greed reading, tracking Bitcoin's pullback. Fund-flow data still reflect the pre-selloff week (cash-into-equities rotation through 16 Sep); the next EPFR/BofA cut lands around 25 Sep and should reveal whether this reversal shows up in flows.

flows.narrative: The freshest available EPFR/BofA weekly data still cover the week ended 16 September: global equity funds absorbed a three-month-high +$62.1bn while money-market funds saw a nine-week-high -$59.5bn redemption, a clear cash-to-equities rotation. Credit was more mixed -- IG inflows slowed to a trickle (+$0.4bn) and HY posted its worst outflow in six months (-$1.9bn) -- while government bonds kept drawing money (+$2.3bn) amid rising rate volatility, and gold ETFs extended a nine-week inflow streak. No newer cut has been published as of this research pass; granular regional equity splits (US/Europe/EM/China/Japan) were not separately disclosed in the secondary sources checked.
